quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! They can also hover in mid-air by flapping their wings in a figure-8 pattern up to 80 times per second. These tiny acrobats visit hundreds of flowers each day, remembering every single one they've been to.

short_read.title: The Secret Language of Trees
short_read.teaser: Scientists have discovered that trees actually communicate with each other through underground fungal networks, sharing nutrients and warning each other of danger. This 'wood wide web' shows that forests are more connected than we ever imagined.

medium_read.title: The Return of Sea Otters to the Pacific Northwest
medium_read.teaser: After nearly disappearing from the Strait of Juan de Fuca, sea otters are making a remarkable comeback thanks to conservation efforts. Their return is transforming kelp forests and bringing the ecosystem back into balance in ways scientists are still discovering.

long_read.title: The Lost Art of Hungarian Embroidery
long_read.teaser: For centuries, Hungarian women passed down intricate embroidery patterns that told stories of their villages and families. This beautiful exploration traces how these folk art traditions are being preserved and celebrated by a new generation of artists.

port_angeles.title: Black-Tailed Deer in Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: August is prime time to spot Olympic black-tailed deer grazing in the wildflower meadows of Hurricane Ridge. These gentle deer are unique to the Pacific Northwest and are often seen with their fawns during late summer. Early morning or late afternoon visits offer the best viewing opportunities.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! You're absolutely right — that tiny heart is working incredibly hard!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute — that's 20 times per second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Those tiny hearts are truly remarkable — they beat about 1,200 times per minute to fuel their incredible flying abilities!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To power their high-energy lifestyle, hummingbirds must eat about half their body weight in sugar every day, visiting hundreds of flowers from dawn to dusk.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderfully done! Pillangó is such a lovely, dancing word for such a lovely, dancing creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' — doesn't it sound like the flutter of wings?
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is part of the Finno-Ugric language family, making it quite different from other European languages. Many Hungarian words are beautifully descriptive and poetic.

puzzle_3.question: What is the Strait of Juan de Fuca named after?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Excellent! Ioannis Phokas was a Greek navigator who sailed for Spain and claimed to have discovered this strait in 1592, though historians still debate whether he actually sailed these waters!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The strait is named after Ioannis Phokas, a Greek navigator sailing under the Spanish name Juan de Fuca. He claimed to have discovered it in 1592, though the strait wasn't verified by Europeans until 200 years later!
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: British captain Charles Barkley is credited with confirming the existence of the strait in 1787 and naming it after Juan de Fuca. The waterway connects the Pacific Ocean to Puget Sound and is about 96 miles long.
